name: Beyoncé
label: Parkwood/Columbia
lede: A nine-year-old at a Houston audition, a girl group that got dropped before its first album, and a run of eight straight No. 1 debuts that ended up at a dance record.

eras.title: Girl's Tyme to Columbia
eras.text: Houston talent shows, a failed Star Search run, a record deal that evaporated, and a father who quit his Xerox job to manage the group. By 1999 the group had a name from the Book of Isaiah and a record that would sell in the millions.

years.h: Nine-year-old Beyoncé meets LaTavia Roberson at an audition
years.p: The audition was for an all-girl group in Houston. [[Kelly Rowland|31bea673-d23a-4889-8da1-7cb040863268]] joined in 1992, and the group worked the local talent circuit as Girl's Tyme.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Beyoncé and LaTavia Roberson met at that audition in 1990, and the trio with Rowland performed rap and dance routines around Houston.

Later names, per Wikipedia's Destiny's Child page, included Somethin' Fresh, Cliché, the Dolls, Borderline and Destiny.

years.h: Girl's Tyme takes the Star Search stage and loses
years.p: Wikipedia's Destiny's Child page says the group was rapping rather than singing. [[LeToya Luckett|b2f1149b-171a-4bc5-ac8f-3baf9a566abf]] joined around this time, making it four.
years.xp: Mathew Knowles, Beyoncé's father, began managing the group. Wikipedia dates his exit from a Xerox sales job to 1995. The Beyoncé and Destiny's Child pages give slightly different years for the Star Search appearance.

years.h: Dropped by Elektra, renamed from the Book of Isaiah, signed by Columbia
years.p: Signed as Destiny, the group was dropped by Elektra before an album appeared. Adopting the name Destiny's Child, it landed at Columbia with help from scout Teresa LaBarbera Whites.

yt: Destiny's Child, Say My Name (official video)
years.h: The Writing's on the Wall gives them two No. 1 singles
years.p: "Bills, Bills, Bills" was their first chart-topper and "Say My Name" went to No. 1 too. Wikipedia says the album sold 13 million copies worldwide.

eras.title: Two out, two in, one lawsuit
eras.text: The group that made it big was not the group that started. The exits made the tabloids, but the records kept going: a record-long No. 1 and an album Beyoncé co-wrote and co-produced for the most part.

years.h: Roberson and Luckett out; Michelle Williams and Farrah Franklin in
years.p: Wikipedia reports that Roberson and Luckett tried to leave Mathew Knowles's management in December 1999. Their replacements arrived in February 2000.
years.xp:
Roberson and Luckett alleged favoritism toward Beyoncé and Rowland, Wikipedia reports. In March 2000 they filed suit against Knowles and their former bandmates.

Farrah Franklin left after five months, per Wikipedia, citing stress and decision-making conflicts. That left Beyoncé, Rowland and [[Michelle Williams|fac0f203-eb89-4d34-a3c5-8e353356d756]] as the trio.

years.h: "Independent Women Part I" sits at No. 1 for 11 weeks
years.p: It ran from November 2000 into January 2001, the longest run of the group's chart-toppers according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Survivor: Beyoncé takes the wheel
years.p: She co-wrote and co-produced most of it, and it debuted at No. 1 with 663,000 first-week sales per Wikipedia. "Bootylicious" reached No. 2.
years.xp: Wikipedia adds that the word "bootylicious" made it into the Oxford English Dictionary in 2006. The group announced a hiatus in 2001 to pursue solo projects.

eras.title: The solo test run, then the goodbye
eras.text: The hiatus was supposed to be a break. Beyoncé left it with a No. 1 album, five Grammys and a rolled-up group she could return to once, in 2004.

q: One of the most compelling instruments in popular music.
Jody Rosen, New York Times Style Magazine
yt: Crazy in Love ft. Jay-Z (official video)
years.h: Dangerously in Love and "Crazy in Love" with Jay-Z
years.p: The single spent eight weeks at No. 1 before the album debuted at No. 1 on June 24 with 317,000 first-week sales. "Baby Boy" stayed at the top for nine weeks.
years.xp:
The record won five Grammys at the 46th ceremony in 2004, including Best Contemporary R&B Album. Wikipedia lists global sales over 11 million.

Jody Rosen, writing for New York Times Style Magazine, is quoted by Wikipedia on her voice.

years.h: Destiny Fulfilled: one last album as a trio
years.p: All three members contributed to the songwriting and served as executive producers. "Lose My Breath" and "Soldier" both reached No. 3.

years.h: Destiny's Child announce the end in Barcelona
years.p: They told the crowd on the tour stop on June 11. A farewell show at the NBA All-Star Game in Houston followed on February 19, 2006.
years.xp: The group's greatest-hits set #1's came out in October 2005, per Wikipedia. Wikipedia counts over 60 million records sold and calls them the best-selling girl group of all time.

eras.title: Irreplaceable
eras.text: The decade's biggest pop star ran two albums in parallel and then took a hiatus nobody expected. Along the way she became the most-awarded woman in a single Grammy night.

years.h: B'Day arrives on her 25th birthday
years.p: It debuted at No. 1 with 541,000 first-week sales, and "Irreplaceable" sat atop the Hot 100 for ten weeks, the top chart hit of 2007 per Wikipedia.
years.xp: "Check on It", from The Pink Panther soundtrack, made her the first woman to hold No. 1 with a film and a single at the same time, Wikipedia says. The album won Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 49th Grammys.

years.h: I Am... Sasha Fierce splits in two: ballads, then club
years.p: The double album's "Single Ladies" was her fifth Hot 100 No. 1 and, per Wikipedia, the first big dance craze of the internet age.
years.xp: "Halo" and "Single Ladies" both went diamond with the RIAA. At the 52nd Grammys in 2010 Beyoncé won six awards, breaking the record for most won by a woman in one night, according to Wikipedia.
play: Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)

years.h: A nine-month hiatus: Great Wall, pyramids, museums
years.p: Beyoncé told the world she would step away from music. Her Essence cover story about it won a writing award from the New York Association of Black Journalists.

eras.title: Her own label, her own rules
eras.text: After her father stopped managing her in 2011, the records and releases got stranger, bolder and entirely hers. The surprise album at the end of 2013 rewrote how big artists drop music.

years.h: 4: a soul record made on her own terms
years.p: After Mathew Knowles stopped managing her in March 2011, this became her first album through her own company, Parkwood Entertainment, and her fourth straight No. 1.

years.h: First solo woman in 20-plus years to headline Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage
years.p: Two days after 4 came out she played the Pyramid Stage, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: A cropped version of the previously uploaded file "FWT11.jpg", which features Beyoncé… · Wikimedia
yt: Beyoncé and Destiny's Child, Super Bowl XLVII halftime
years.h: Super Bowl XLVII: Beyoncé headlines, Destiny's Child reunite
years.p: She headlined the halftime show in New Orleans with Rowland and Williams joining her. Wikipedia calls it the second most-tweeted moment in history at the time.

years.h: Beyoncé: a visual album on iTunes, no announcement
years.p: Fifth studio album, fifth No. 1 debut, with 617,000 first-week sales per Wikipedia. The music videos were recorded in secret.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits the release with pushing the record industry's global release day to Friday, adopted by the IFPI.

"Drunk in Love", with Jay-Z, peaked at No. 2 and won two Grammys. The album explores marriage, motherhood, postnatal depression and bulimia, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Lemonade, Coachella, Homecoming
eras.text: Beyoncé made films, stage shows and albums that were treated as events. Each one set the next one's bar.

years.h: "Formation" drops, then Beyoncé plays it at Super Bowl 50
years.p: Wikipedia notes that the halftime set drew controversy over perceived Black Panther Party allusions.

years.h: Lemonade premieres on HBO and Tidal the same night
years.p: An hour-long film on HBO, the album exclusive to Tidal. It debuted at No. 1 with 653,000 first-week sales, her sixth straight No. 1 debut, and all 12 tracks charted on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
"Sorry", "Hold Up", "Freedom" and "All Night" were singles. The Formation World Tour ran April to October 2016 and was the first all-stadium tour by a woman, Wikipedia says.

Beyoncé won eight awards at that year's MTV VMAs, including Video of the Year for "Formation". Lemonade won Best Urban Contemporary Album at the 2017 Grammys.

years.cap: The world's biggest girl pop group, Destiny's child. Beyonce Knowles 19, Photographed in… · Wikimedia
years.h: Coachella: two weekends, HBCU marching bands, Destiny's Child cameo
years.p: Wikipedia calls the April 14 set the most-watched live performance on YouTube up to then.
years.xp: The show paid homage to Black culture and HBCUs, per Wikipedia. Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams came on for the Destiny's Child moment. The film Homecoming reached Netflix on April 17, 2019, with a live album, and earned six Emmy nominations.

years.h: Everything Is Love: a full album with Jay-Z as the Carters
years.p: It came out mid-way through their On the Run II tour. Wikipedia reports a No. 2 debut with 123,000 album-equivalent units; "Apeshit" reached No. 13.

years.h: Nala in The Lion King, plus a companion album called The Gift
years.p: She curated The Lion King: The Gift with African producers, folding in gqom and Afrobeat. A visual companion, Black Is King, followed in July 2020.

eras.title: The house record
eras.text: After the pandemic, Beyoncé picked up disco and house, the music of Black queer clubs, and made it the first installment of a trilogy. The response was close to unanimous.

years.h: Most-awarded singer and woman in Grammy history
years.p: She led the 63rd Grammys with nine nominations and won four. Wikipedia puts her second overall among all people.

years.h: "Break My Soul" becomes her eighth Hot 100 No. 1
years.p: She announced Renaissance on June 16 and dropped the lead single four days later.

years.h: Renaissance: Pitchfork gives it 9.0, No. 1 of 2022
years.p: Pitchfork's review scored the album 9.0 and its year-end list put it first. Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 91 from 26 reviews.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits producers The-Dream, Honey Dijon, Skrillex, Mike Dean, Hit-Boy and others. Grace Jones, Tems and Beam feature. Samples include Big Freedia, Right Said Fred, Robin S. and the Clark Sisters.

The album leaked on July 27 when French retailers shipped copies early. All 16 tracks charted on the Hot 100, and "Cuff It" peaked at No. 6 and became her longest-charting single.

years.h: Beyoncé removes a word from "Heated" the day after release
years.p: Disability advocates had objected to it as a slur. Beyoncé announced on August 1 she would replace it.
years.xp: Wikipedia's page on the song notes some listeners said the word means something different in African-American English, but that advocates held to the objection. Wikipedia also notes Kelis objected to the interpolation of "Milkshake" on "Energy".

eras.title: The tour, then the country record
eras.text: She toured Renaissance across the world, then turned to Americana. The Grammys answered that move with the top prize.

years.h: The Renaissance World Tour grosses over $579 million
years.p: Wikipedia calls it the highest-grossing tour by a woman and by a Black artist. A concert film of it followed.
years.xp:
She also won four of her nine nominations at the 65th Grammys, including Best Dance/Electronic Album for Renaissance, and became the most-awarded artist in Grammy history, Wikipedia says.

Wikipedia's Beyoncé page dates the film to November 2023, its album page to December 1.

years.h: Cowboy Carter: Americana and overlooked Black country pioneers
years.p: "Texas Hold 'Em" gave her a ninth Hot 100 No. 1 before release. The album debuted at No. 1 with 407,000 first-week sales, her eighth in a row.
years.xp: "II Most Wanted", with Miley Cyrus, debuted at No. 6. The Cowboy Carter Tour became the highest-grossing country tour ever, Wikipedia says.

years.h: Cowboy Carter wins Album of the Year and Best Country Album
years.p: She was the first Black artist to win Best Country Album, and the first Black woman in 26 years to take Album of the Year, Wikipedia says.

years.h: "Morning Dew (Donk)" appears without warning
years.p: A 20th-anniversary edition of B'Day with unreleased tracks followed on September 4, 2026, per Wikipedia.
